The *Paṇṇattivāraniddesa* (Ya 3.1.2) is an Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It serves as the full exposition (*niddesa*) of the designation section (*paṇṇattivāra*) within the third major chapter of the *Yamaka* [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in one language for this text [SuttaCentral].

According to computational analysis by DharmaNexus, the *Paṇṇattivāraniddesa* exhibits dense internal text reuse across the Pali canon and post-canonical literature, sharing 1,953 matching passages across 49 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Yamaka*, it shares substantial formulaic and doctrinal material with its introductory summary section, the *Paṇṇattivārauddesa* (Ya 3.1.1), adjacent sections including the *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 3.2.2), *Uppādavāra* (Ya 3.2.1), and *Uppādanirodhavāra* (Ya 3.2.3), and corresponding *paṇṇattivāra* expositions elsewhere in the book (Ya 2.1.2, Ya 4.1.2, Ya 5.1.2, Ya 9.1.2, and Ya 10.1.2) [DharmaNexus]. Substantial overlaps also connect it to the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi*, the *Rūpavibhatti* of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* (Ds 2.2.3), the *Āyatanavibhaṅga* (Vb 2), and the *Visuddhimagga* and its *Mahāṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments automatically with Tibetan translations of Sanskrit Buddhist texts, including Prajñāpāramitā literature (*Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā* and *Śatasāhasrikā*) and Abhidharma/Yogācāra treatises such as the *Pañcaskandhaprakaraṇa*, *Pañcaskandhabhāṣya*, *Yogācārabhūmiviniścayasaṃgrahaṇī*, and *Abhidharmasamuccayabhāṣya* [DharmaNexus].
